900100.title: The 1:1 World
900100.summary: Life-size and larger: entering true macro.

details.subject: The 1:1 World
details.note: True macro begins at 1:1 — the subject rendered life-size on the sensor — and the world changes at that magnification. The depth of field collapses to millimeters, the light falls off a cliff, and the familiar becomes alien. The technique is the tripod and the rail: at 1:1 the camera moves in millimeters, and the focusing rail is the steering wheel. The subject discipline is the stillness — the macro photographer learns to shoot between breaths and breezes. The 1:1 world's lesson is scale: the tiny is vast if you get close enough. The sensor is the window; the magnification is the journey.
key_points: Depth of field collapses to millimeters.
Tripod plus focusing rail for control.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The 1:1 World

details.subject: Focus Stacking Deep
details.note: Focus stacking defeats macro's cruelest limit: the millimeter-deep depth of field. The technique shoots a stack of frames, each focused a hair deeper, and software fuses the sharp slices into one impossibly deep image. The capture discipline is the step size — overlap the slices generously, because gaps become blur bands. The subject must be perfectly still across the stack: the technique is for the patient and the windless. The stacking lesson is computational photography's promise — the camera captures the data, the software builds the image. The stack is the exposure; the fusion is the photograph.
key_points: Shoot a stack, each focused deeper.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Focus Stacking Deep

900102.title: The Six-Legged Sitter
900102.summary: Six legs and a face: photographing insects.

details.subject: The Six-Legged Sitter
details.note: The insect portrait treats the bug as a sitter: the compound eyes, the mandibles, the iridescent armor — a face worth framing. The field craft is the approach: move slowly, shoot early when the cold slows them, and never chase. The lighting is the diffused flash — the softbox on a stick that turns harsh noon into studio light. The ethics are the leave-no-trace: photograph the wild, don't stage it. The insect portrait's reward is the alien familiar — the creature you've ignored becomes a character. The lens is the introduction; the patience is the conversation.
key_points: Approach slowly; shoot the cold morning.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Six-Legged Sitter

900103.title: Dewdrop Universes
900103.summary: Worlds in a drop: the dewdrop refraction.

details.subject: Dewdrop Universes
details.note: The dewdrop holds a universe: each bead refracts the world behind it into a tiny inverted lens. The technique is the alignment — the camera, the drop, and the background flower must line up, and the drop does the optics. The timing is the dawn: the drops form overnight and vanish with the sun, so the macro photographer works the blue hour. The background discipline is the bokeh garden — the refracted image needs a luminous backdrop to read. The dewdrop's lesson is the found lens: nature builds optics better than factories. The drop is the lens; the dawn is the studio.
key_points: Work the dawn before drops vanish.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Dewdrop Universes

900104.title: The Texture Microscope
900104.summary: Bark, rust, and stone: the texture survey.

details.subject: The Texture Microscope
details.note: The texture survey photographs the world's surfaces at macro range: bark becomes canyon, rust becomes nebula, stone becomes moonscape. The technique is the raking light — light from the side reveals the relief that flat light hides. The subject discipline is the wander: the texture photographer walks slowly, scanning surfaces for the square inch that sings. The composition is the abstraction — frame tight enough that the subject becomes pattern. The survey's lesson is the everywhere — the extraordinary hides in the ordinary at 1:1. The surface is the subject; the light is the reveal.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Texture Microscope

900105.title: Lighting the Tiny
900105.summary: Studio light for small subjects: the macro lighting kit.

details.subject: Lighting the Tiny
details.note: Lighting the tiny is macro's central craft: the small subject needs soft, close, controllable light. The kit is the diffused flash, the LED panel, and the reflector card — the holy trinity of macro illumination. The technique is the closeness: the light must be near the subject, because small lights far away are hard lights. The discipline is the ratio — the key light shapes, the fill light lifts, and the tiny subject gets the full studio treatment. The lighting lesson is the scale truth: light behaves the same at every size, but the fixtures must shrink. The subject is small; the lighting is not.
key_points: Diffused flash, LED panel, reflector card.
Light close: small far lights are hard.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lighting the Tiny

900106.title: The Flower's Architecture
900106.summary: Petals as buildings: the floral macro.

details.subject: The Flower's Architecture
details.note: The flower's architecture reveals at macro range: the petal's veins become buttresses, the stamen becomes a tower, the pollen becomes gold dust. The technique is the bloom schedule — shoot the flower at its peak, in the cool morning before the petals wilt. The composition is the architecture: find the leading lines of the veins, the symmetry of the reproductive parts, the geometry of the bloom. The background discipline is the clean wash — the wide aperture melts the garden into color. The floral macro's lesson is the engineering: the flower is a machine for pollination, beautiful by function. The bloom is the building; the bee is the client.
key_points: Shoot the peak bloom, cool morning.
Compose on the veins' leading lines.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Flower's Architecture

details.subject: Abstract Macro
details.note: Abstract macro leaves recognition behind: the subject becomes color, line, and texture, and the photograph is pure form. The technique is the fragment — frame so tight the object's identity dissolves. The subject hunting is the play: oil on water, soap films, crystal growths, the accidents that make art. The lighting is the drama: the abstract lives on contrast and glow. The abstract lesson is the seeing: the macro photographer learns to see the photograph before the subject. The frame is the art; the subject is the excuse.
key_points: See the photograph before the subject.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Abstract Macro

900108.title: The Macro Lens Guide
900108.summary: Choosing the glass: the macro lens survey.

details.subject: The Macro Lens Guide
details.note: The macro lens guide surveys the glass: the 60mm for the studio, the 100mm for the field, the 180mm for the shy. The choosing criteria are the working distance — the space between lens and subject — and the magnification, honestly rated. The technique note is the manual focus: at macro range the autofocus hunts, and the photographer's hand is the better motor. The budget wisdom is the extension tube: the cheap tube turns any lens macro-ish, and the craft matters more than the glass. The guide's lesson is the sufficiency: one good macro lens, learned deeply, beats the cabinet. The lens is the tool; the eye is the instrument.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Macro Lens Guide

900109.title: The Patient Photographer
900109.summary: The capstone: macro as a meditation.

details.subject: The Patient Photographer
details.note: The patient photographer is macro's capstone: the craft's final lesson is that the photographer's stillness matters more than the gear. The practice is the wait — the insect will turn, the light will shift, the drop will form, and the photographer who waits gets the frame. The discipline is the breath: the macro shooter learns to release the shutter between heartbeats. The philosophy is the attention: macro photography is sustained looking, and the looking changes the looker. The capstone's truth is the exchange — the tiny world gives its portrait to those who pay attention. The patience is the lens. The attention is the photograph.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Patient Photographer

900110.title: The Exposure Triangle
900110.summary: Aperture, shutter, ISO: the foundational lesson.

details.subject: The Exposure Triangle
details.note: The exposure triangle is photography's first lesson: aperture, shutter speed, and ISO in eternal negotiation. The teaching is the triangle's trade — open the aperture and the shutter must quicken; slow the shutter and the ISO must fall. The exercise is the same scene three ways: the deep-focus landscape, the frozen motion, the clean low-light — each a different corner of the triangle. The student's breakthrough is the priority modes: aperture priority for the depth thinker, shutter priority for the motion thinker. The triangle's lesson is the exposure as a decision — the camera can choose, but the photographer should. The triangle is the grammar; the photograph is the sentence.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Exposure Triangle

900111.title: Lesson: Composition First
900111.summary: Before the settings: seeing the frame.

details.subject: Lesson: Composition First
details.note: Composition first is the school's founding rule: the frame matters more than the settings. The lesson teaches the seeing — the rule of thirds, the leading lines, the foreground interest — before the camera leaves auto. The exercise is the viewfinder walk: frame a hundred scenes without pressing the shutter, and the eye learns faster than the finger. The student's breakthrough is the exclusion: composition is what you leave out. The lesson's truth is the hierarchy — a well-composed phone photo beats a poorly composed masterpiece of exposure. The frame is the photograph; the settings are the footnotes.
key_points: The viewfinder walk: frame without shooting.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Composition First

900112.title: Lesson: Light Is the Subject
900112.summary: The real subject of every photograph.

details.subject: Lesson: Light Is the Subject
details.note: Light is the subject is the school's central doctrine: the photograph is never of the thing, it's of the light on the thing. The lesson teaches the light's qualities — the direction, the color, the hardness — and how each transforms the mundane. The exercise is the same object all day: photograph the chair at dawn, noon, and dusk, and watch three photographs emerge. The student's breakthrough is the golden hour's demotion: beautiful light is everywhere, once you learn to see it. The lesson's truth is the photographer's real hunt — we don't chase subjects, we chase light. The thing is the excuse; the light is the subject.
key_points: The photo is of the light, not the thing.
Same object, three lights, three photos.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Light Is the Subject

900113.title: Lesson: The Decisive Moment
900113.summary: Timing as a discipline: the Cartier-Bresson lesson.

details.subject: Lesson: The Decisive Moment
details.note: The decisive moment teaches timing as a discipline: the photograph happens when the elements align, and the photographer's job is to be ready. The lesson teaches the anticipation — read the scene, predict the convergence, and pre-focus the spot. The exercise is the street corner: pick the background, wait for the foreground, and shoot the meeting. The student's breakthrough is the patience: the decisive moment is mostly waiting, briefly shooting. The lesson's truth is the readiness — the camera set, the eye open, the finger light. The moment is the photograph; the waiting is the craft.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: The Decisive Moment

900114.title: Lesson: Portraiture Basics
900114.summary: The face, respected: the portrait lesson.

details.subject: Lesson: Portraiture Basics
details.note: Portraiture basics teach the face respected: the connection before the capture. The lesson teaches the light's kindness — the large soft source, the flattering angle — and the direction's clarity. The exercise is the ten-minute portrait: one sitter, one window, ten frames, and the conversation matters more than the settings. The student's breakthrough is the eyes: the focus belongs on the near eye, always. The lesson's truth is the sitter's comfort — the relaxed face photographs, the tense face poses. The portrait is the relationship; the camera is the witness.
key_points: One window, ten frames, real conversation.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Portraiture Basics

900115.title: Lesson: Editing with Intent
900115.summary: The darkroom's discipline: edit like you mean it.

details.subject: Lesson: Editing with Intent
details.note: Editing with intent teaches the darkroom's discipline: every slider serves the photograph's idea. The lesson teaches the restraint — the edit should be invisible, serving the image rather than announcing itself. The exercise is the before-and-after: edit the same raw three ways (faithful, dramatic, wrong) and feel the difference intent makes. The student's breakthrough is the crop: the edit begins with the frame, and most photographs improve by subtraction. The lesson's truth is the honesty — the edit clarifies what was seen; it doesn't invent what wasn't. The raw is the negative; the edit is the print.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Editing with Intent

900116.title: Lesson: The Photo Walk
900116.summary: The practice field: walking with a camera.

details.subject: Lesson: The Photo Walk
details.note: The photo walk is the school's practice field: the camera, the street, and the assignment. The lesson teaches the constraint — one lens, one theme, one hour — because limits teach faster than freedom. The exercise is the themed walk: shadows, or doors, or the color red, and the street becomes the syllabus. The student's breakthrough is the return: walk the same route monthly, and the photographs track the eye's growth. The lesson's truth is the mileage — the photographer is made by the walking. The street is the school; the walk is the lesson.
key_points: Constraint: one lens, one theme, one hour.
Themed walks make the street a syllabus.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: The Photo Walk

900117.title: Lesson: Critique Without Cruelty
900117.summary: Growing through feedback: the critique method.

details.subject: Lesson: Critique Without Cruelty
details.note: Critique without cruelty teaches the feedback that grows: the method is the sandwich's honest cousin — the observation, the question, the suggestion. The lesson teaches the vocabulary: talk about the light, the frame, the moment — the photograph's elements, not the photographer's worth. The exercise is the group crit: each photographer presents, each viewer responds with one noticing and one wondering. The student's breakthrough is the receiving: the critique is data, not verdict. The lesson's truth is the kindness's rigor — the gentle critique can be the most exacting. The feedback is the gift; the cruelty is the theft.
key_points: Kindness can be the most exacting.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Critique Without Cruelty

900118.title: Lesson: The Personal Project
900118.summary: The long work: photographing one thing deeply.

details.subject: Lesson: The Personal Project
details.note: The personal project teaches the long work: one subject, photographed deeply over months. The lesson teaches the commitment — the project survives the boring middle, where the novelty fades and the seeing deepens. The exercise is the hundred-frame project: one subject, a hundred frames, the edit to twelve. The student's breakthrough is the theme's emergence: the project teaches the photographer what they actually care about. The lesson's truth is the depth's reward — the hundredth frame sees what the first couldn't. The project is the education; the subject is the teacher.
key_points: The theme emerges from the work.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: The Personal Project

details.subject: Graduation: Your First Exhibition
details.note: Graduation is the first exhibition: the work leaves the hard drive and meets the wall. The lesson teaches the edit — the show is twelve prints, not the archive, and the sequence is the argument. The craft is the print: the paper, the size, the frame, each a decision about how the photograph wants to be seen. The exercise is the hanging: the work on the wall, the artist's statement beside it, the opening with real viewers. The student's breakthrough is the public: the photograph completes itself in the viewer's eye. The graduation's truth is the threshold — the exhibitor is no longer just a student. The wall is the diploma.
key_points: Twelve prints, sequenced as an argument.
The photograph completes in the viewer.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Graduation: Your First Exhibition

900120.title: The Blue Hour Hunt
900120.summary: The twenty minutes of blue: the twilight hunt.

details.subject: The Blue Hour Hunt
details.note: The blue hour hunt chases the twenty minutes after sunset: the sky goes cobalt, the city lights ignite, and the world balances. The technique is the tripod and the patience — the blue hour's light fades fast, so the compositions are found before the color peaks. The subject discipline is the silhouette and the glow: the hunt favors the skyline, the lit window, the streetlamp's halo. The exposure craft is the balance — the sky and the lights in one frame, neither blown nor buried. The hunt's lesson is the daily miracle: the blue hour happens every day, and most people miss it. The camera is the excuse to watch. The blue is the reward.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Blue Hour Hunt

900121.title: The Minimalist Hunt
900121.summary: Less, but better: the minimalist hunt.

details.subject: The Minimalist Hunt
details.note: The minimalist hunt seeks the essential: one subject, clean space, nothing extra. The technique is the subtraction — the hunter frames out the clutter until the photograph breathes. The subject discipline is the single note: the lone tree, the one bird, the empty bench — each carrying the frame alone. The composition craft is the negative space: the emptiness is the subject's stage. The hunt's lesson is the confidence: the minimalist frame trusts the viewer to feel the quiet. The less is the more; the space is the statement.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Minimalist Hunt

900122.title: The Leading Lines Hunt
900122.summary: Follow the lines: the geometry hunt.

details.subject: The Leading Lines Hunt
details.note: The leading lines hunt follows the geometry: the road, the railing, the shoreline — every line that pulls the eye. The technique is the alignment — the hunter positions so the lines converge on the subject. The subject discipline is the anchor: the lines need a destination, the payoff at the vanishing point. The composition craft is the diagonal's energy — the tilted line moves, the horizontal rests. The hunt's lesson is the eye's obedience: the viewer follows lines involuntarily, and the photographer conducts. The lines are the leash; the subject is the reward.
key_points: Align lines to converge on subject.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Leading Lines Hunt

900123.title: The Human Element Hunt
900123.summary: The figure in the landscape: the scale hunt.

details.subject: The Human Element Hunt
details.note: The human element hunt places the figure in the landscape: the tiny silhouette that gives the vast its scale. The technique is the patience — the hunter frames the scene and waits for the walker. The subject discipline is the scale: the figure must be small enough to humble, large enough to read. The composition craft is the placement — the figure on the third, the landscape doing the rest. The hunt's lesson is the story: the figure turns the landscape into a narrative. The vast is the setting; the human is the plot.
key_points: Frame the scene; wait for the walker.
Small enough to humble, large to read.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Human Element Hunt

900124.title: The Symmetry Hunt
900124.summary: The mirrored world: the symmetry hunt.

details.subject: The Symmetry Hunt
details.note: The symmetry hunt seeks the mirrored world: the reflection, the facade, the perfect bilateral. The technique is the centering — the symmetry demands the axis dead-center. The subject discipline is the water: the still pond, the polished floor, the glass tower — the surfaces that double the world. The composition craft is the break — the best symmetries include the flaw, the bird on the wire that proves it's real. The hunt's lesson is the order: the symmetrical frame satisfies like a resolved chord. The mirror is the subject; the flaw is the signature.
key_points: Include the flaw that proves it's real.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Symmetry Hunt

details.subject: The Motion Blur Hunt
details.note: The motion blur hunt smears the speed: the slow shutter turns the rushing world into streaks. The technique is the drag — the shutter slow enough to blur, the camera steady enough to anchor. The subject discipline is the contrast: the sharp still against the blurred rush — the statue and the crowd. The composition craft is the pan — follow the subject and the background becomes the blur. The hunt's lesson is the time made visible: the photograph shows the duration, not the instant. The blur is the truth; the sharp is the anchor.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Motion Blur Hunt

900126.title: The Frame Within a Frame
900126.summary: Doorways and windows: the nested hunt.

details.subject: The Frame Within a Frame
details.note: The frame within a frame hunt nests the composition: the doorway, the window, the arch — each a frame around the frame. The technique is the layering — the hunter finds the foreground frame that organizes the scene. The subject discipline is the depth: the nested frames create the tunnel the eye travels. The composition craft is the darkness — the frame's shadow makes the inner image glow. The hunt's lesson is the organization: the frame tames the chaos. The doorway is the viewfinder; the world is the photograph.
key_points: The frame's shadow makes images glow.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Frame Within a Frame

900127.title: The High Contrast Hunt
900127.summary: Black and white thinking: the contrast hunt.

details.subject: The High Contrast Hunt
details.note: The high contrast hunt thinks in black and white: the harsh light, the deep shadow, the graphic frame. The technique is the exposure for the highlights — the hunter lets the shadows fall where they may. The subject discipline is the graphic: the hunt favors the bold shape, the strong line, the unapologetic dark. The composition craft is the abstraction — the contrast reduces the world to design. The hunt's lesson is the light's edge: the harsh light that ruins the portrait makes the graphic. The shadow is the ink; the light is the paper.
key_points: Favor bold shapes and strong lines.
Contrast reduces the world to design.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The High Contrast Hunt

900128.title: The Quiet Moment Hunt
900128.summary: The pause between: the quiet hunt.

details.subject: The Quiet Moment Hunt
details.note: The quiet moment hunt seeks the pause between: the empty chair, the folded hands, the held breath. The technique is the invisibility — the hunter becomes furniture, and the moment arrives unposed. The subject discipline is the small: the quiet lives in the details, not the spectacles. The composition craft is the restraint — the quiet frame whispers. The hunt's lesson is the attention: the quiet moments are everywhere, and the camera teaches the noticing. The pause is the photograph; the noticing is the hunt.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Quiet Moment Hunt

900129.title: The Panorama Hunt
900129.summary: The wide world: the panoramic hunt.

details.subject: The Panorama Hunt
details.note: The panorama hunt takes the wide world: the vista too broad for one frame, stitched from many. The technique is the overlap — the hunter shoots the sequence with generous overlap, level and steady. The subject discipline is the horizon: the panorama needs the line that holds it together. The composition craft is the ends — the panorama's edges must earn their place. The hunt's lesson is the breadth: the wide frame teaches the wide seeing. The Year of Hunts closes with the widest view. The vista is the subject; the stitching is the craft.
key_points: The wide frame teaches wide seeing.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Panorama Hunt

JAH-PHO-010056.summary: Aperture, shutter, ISO: the foundational lesson.

details.subject: The Exposure Triangle
details.note: The exposure triangle is photography's first lesson: aperture, shutter speed, and ISO in eternal negotiation. The teaching is the triangle's trade — open the aperture and the shutter must quicken; slow the shutter and the ISO must fall. The exercise is the same scene three ways: the deep-focus landscape, the frozen motion, the clean low-light — each a different corner of the triangle. The student's breakthrough is the priority modes: aperture priority for the depth thinker, shutter priority for the motion thinker. The triangle's lesson is the exposure as a decision — the camera can choose, but the photographer should. The triangle is the grammar; the photograph is the sentence.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Exposure Triangle

JAH-PHO-010057.title: Lesson: Composition First
JAH-PHO-010057.summary: Before the settings: seeing the frame.

details.subject: Lesson: Composition First
details.note: Composition first is the school's founding rule: the frame matters more than the settings. The lesson teaches the seeing — the rule of thirds, the leading lines, the foreground interest — before the camera leaves auto. The exercise is the viewfinder walk: frame a hundred scenes without pressing the shutter, and the eye learns faster than the finger. The student's breakthrough is the exclusion: composition is what you leave out. The lesson's truth is the hierarchy — a well-composed phone photo beats a poorly composed masterpiece of exposure. The frame is the photograph; the settings are the footnotes.
key_points: The viewfinder walk: frame without shooting.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Composition First

JAH-PHO-010058.title: Lesson: Light Is the Subject
JAH-PHO-010058.summary: The real subject of every photograph.

details.subject: Lesson: Light Is the Subject
details.note: Light is the subject is the school's central doctrine: the photograph is never of the thing, it's of the light on the thing. The lesson teaches the light's qualities — the direction, the color, the hardness — and how each transforms the mundane. The exercise is the same object all day: photograph the chair at dawn, noon, and dusk, and watch three photographs emerge. The student's breakthrough is the golden hour's demotion: beautiful light is everywhere, once you learn to see it. The lesson's truth is the photographer's real hunt — we don't chase subjects, we chase light. The thing is the excuse; the light is the subject.
key_points: The photo is of the light, not the thing.
Same object, three lights, three photos.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Light Is the Subject

JAH-PHO-010059.title: Lesson: The Decisive Moment
JAH-PHO-010059.summary: Timing as a discipline: the Cartier-Bresson lesson.

details.subject: Lesson: The Decisive Moment
details.note: The decisive moment teaches timing as a discipline: the photograph happens when the elements align, and the photographer's job is to be ready. The lesson teaches the anticipation — read the scene, predict the convergence, and pre-focus the spot. The exercise is the street corner: pick the background, wait for the foreground, and shoot the meeting. The student's breakthrough is the patience: the decisive moment is mostly waiting, briefly shooting. The lesson's truth is the readiness — the camera set, the eye open, the finger light. The moment is the photograph; the waiting is the craft.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: The Decisive Moment

JAH-PHO-010060.title: Lesson: Portraiture Basics
JAH-PHO-010060.summary: The face, respected: the portrait lesson.

details.subject: Lesson: Portraiture Basics
details.note: Portraiture basics teach the face respected: the connection before the capture. The lesson teaches the light's kindness — the large soft source, the flattering angle — and the direction's clarity. The exercise is the ten-minute portrait: one sitter, one window, ten frames, and the conversation matters more than the settings. The student's breakthrough is the eyes: the focus belongs on the near eye, always. The lesson's truth is the sitter's comfort — the relaxed face photographs, the tense face poses. The portrait is the relationship; the camera is the witness.
key_points: One window, ten frames, real conversation.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Portraiture Basics

JAH-PHO-010061.title: Lesson: Editing with Intent
JAH-PHO-010061.summary: The darkroom's discipline: edit like you mean it.

details.subject: Lesson: Editing with Intent
details.note: Editing with intent teaches the darkroom's discipline: every slider serves the photograph's idea. The lesson teaches the restraint — the edit should be invisible, serving the image rather than announcing itself. The exercise is the before-and-after: edit the same raw three ways (faithful, dramatic, wrong) and feel the difference intent makes. The student's breakthrough is the crop: the edit begins with the frame, and most photographs improve by subtraction. The lesson's truth is the honesty — the edit clarifies what was seen; it doesn't invent what wasn't. The raw is the negative; the edit is the print.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Editing with Intent

JAH-PHO-010062.title: Lesson: The Photo Walk
JAH-PHO-010062.summary: The practice field: walking with a camera.

details.subject: Lesson: The Photo Walk
details.note: The photo walk is the school's practice field: the camera, the street, and the assignment. The lesson teaches the constraint — one lens, one theme, one hour — because limits teach faster than freedom. The exercise is the themed walk: shadows, or doors, or the color red, and the street becomes the syllabus. The student's breakthrough is the return: walk the same route monthly, and the photographs track the eye's growth. The lesson's truth is the mileage — the photographer is made by the walking. The street is the school; the walk is the lesson.
key_points: Constraint: one lens, one theme, one hour.
Themed walks make the street a syllabus.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: The Photo Walk

JAH-PHO-010063.title: Lesson: Critique Without Cruelty
JAH-PHO-010063.summary: Growing through feedback: the critique method.

details.subject: Lesson: Critique Without Cruelty
details.note: Critique without cruelty teaches the feedback that grows: the method is the sandwich's honest cousin — the observation, the question, the suggestion. The lesson teaches the vocabulary: talk about the light, the frame, the moment — the photograph's elements, not the photographer's worth. The exercise is the group crit: each photographer presents, each viewer responds with one noticing and one wondering. The student's breakthrough is the receiving: the critique is data, not verdict. The lesson's truth is the kindness's rigor — the gentle critique can be the most exacting. The feedback is the gift; the cruelty is the theft.
key_points: Kindness can be the most exacting.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: Critique Without Cruelty

JAH-PHO-010064.title: Lesson: The Personal Project
JAH-PHO-010064.summary: The long work: photographing one thing deeply.

details.subject: Lesson: The Personal Project
details.note: The personal project teaches the long work: one subject, photographed deeply over months. The lesson teaches the commitment — the project survives the boring middle, where the novelty fades and the seeing deepens. The exercise is the hundred-frame project: one subject, a hundred frames, the edit to twelve. The student's breakthrough is the theme's emergence: the project teaches the photographer what they actually care about. The lesson's truth is the depth's reward — the hundredth frame sees what the first couldn't. The project is the education; the subject is the teacher.
key_points: The theme emerges from the work.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Lesson: The Personal Project

details.subject: Graduation: Your First Exhibition
details.note: Graduation is the first exhibition: the work leaves the hard drive and meets the wall. The lesson teaches the edit — the show is twelve prints, not the archive, and the sequence is the argument. The craft is the print: the paper, the size, the frame, each a decision about how the photograph wants to be seen. The exercise is the hanging: the work on the wall, the artist's statement beside it, the opening with real viewers. The student's breakthrough is the public: the photograph completes itself in the viewer's eye. The graduation's truth is the threshold — the exhibitor is no longer just a student. The wall is the diploma.
key_points: Twelve prints, sequenced as an argument.
The photograph completes in the viewer.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - Graduation: Your First Exhibition

JAH-PHO-010066.title: The Blue Hour Hunt
JAH-PHO-010066.summary: The twenty minutes of blue: the twilight hunt.

details.subject: The Blue Hour Hunt
details.note: The blue hour hunt chases the twenty minutes after sunset: the sky goes cobalt, the city lights ignite, and the world balances. The technique is the tripod and the patience — the blue hour's light fades fast, so the compositions are found before the color peaks. The subject discipline is the silhouette and the glow: the hunt favors the skyline, the lit window, the streetlamp's halo. The exposure craft is the balance — the sky and the lights in one frame, neither blown nor buried. The hunt's lesson is the daily miracle: the blue hour happens every day, and most people miss it. The camera is the excuse to watch. The blue is the reward.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Blue Hour Hunt

JAH-PHO-010067.title: The Minimalist Hunt
JAH-PHO-010067.summary: Less, but better: the minimalist hunt.

details.subject: The Minimalist Hunt
details.note: The minimalist hunt seeks the essential: one subject, clean space, nothing extra. The technique is the subtraction — the hunter frames out the clutter until the photograph breathes. The subject discipline is the single note: the lone tree, the one bird, the empty bench — each carrying the frame alone. The composition craft is the negative space: the emptiness is the subject's stage. The hunt's lesson is the confidence: the minimalist frame trusts the viewer to feel the quiet. The less is the more; the space is the statement.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Minimalist Hunt

JAH-PHO-010068.title: The Leading Lines Hunt
JAH-PHO-010068.summary: Follow the lines: the geometry hunt.

details.subject: The Leading Lines Hunt
details.note: The leading lines hunt follows the geometry: the road, the railing, the shoreline — every line that pulls the eye. The technique is the alignment — the hunter positions so the lines converge on the subject. The subject discipline is the anchor: the lines need a destination, the payoff at the vanishing point. The composition craft is the diagonal's energy — the tilted line moves, the horizontal rests. The hunt's lesson is the eye's obedience: the viewer follows lines involuntarily, and the photographer conducts. The lines are the leash; the subject is the reward.
key_points: Align lines to converge on subject.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Leading Lines Hunt

JAH-PHO-010069.title: The Human Element Hunt
JAH-PHO-010069.summary: The figure in the landscape: the scale hunt.

details.subject: The Human Element Hunt
details.note: The human element hunt places the figure in the landscape: the tiny silhouette that gives the vast its scale. The technique is the patience — the hunter frames the scene and waits for the walker. The subject discipline is the scale: the figure must be small enough to humble, large enough to read. The composition craft is the placement — the figure on the third, the landscape doing the rest. The hunt's lesson is the story: the figure turns the landscape into a narrative. The vast is the setting; the human is the plot.
key_points: Frame the scene; wait for the walker.
Small enough to humble, large to read.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Human Element Hunt

JAH-PHO-010070.title: The Symmetry Hunt
JAH-PHO-010070.summary: The mirrored world: the symmetry hunt.

details.subject: The Symmetry Hunt
details.note: The symmetry hunt seeks the mirrored world: the reflection, the facade, the perfect bilateral. The technique is the centering — the symmetry demands the axis dead-center. The subject discipline is the water: the still pond, the polished floor, the glass tower — the surfaces that double the world. The composition craft is the break — the best symmetries include the flaw, the bird on the wire that proves it's real. The hunt's lesson is the order: the symmetrical frame satisfies like a resolved chord. The mirror is the subject; the flaw is the signature.
key_points: Include the flaw that proves it's real.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Symmetry Hunt

details.subject: The Motion Blur Hunt
details.note: The motion blur hunt smears the speed: the slow shutter turns the rushing world into streaks. The technique is the drag — the shutter slow enough to blur, the camera steady enough to anchor. The subject discipline is the contrast: the sharp still against the blurred rush — the statue and the crowd. The composition craft is the pan — follow the subject and the background becomes the blur. The hunt's lesson is the time made visible: the photograph shows the duration, not the instant. The blur is the truth; the sharp is the anchor.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Motion Blur Hunt

JAH-PHO-010072.title: The Frame Within a Frame
JAH-PHO-010072.summary: Doorways and windows: the nested hunt.

details.subject: The Frame Within a Frame
details.note: The frame within a frame hunt nests the composition: the doorway, the window, the arch — each a frame around the frame. The technique is the layering — the hunter finds the foreground frame that organizes the scene. The subject discipline is the depth: the nested frames create the tunnel the eye travels. The composition craft is the darkness — the frame's shadow makes the inner image glow. The hunt's lesson is the organization: the frame tames the chaos. The doorway is the viewfinder; the world is the photograph.
key_points: The frame's shadow makes images glow.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Frame Within a Frame

JAH-PHO-010073.title: The High Contrast Hunt
JAH-PHO-010073.summary: Black and white thinking: the contrast hunt.

details.subject: The High Contrast Hunt
details.note: The high contrast hunt thinks in black and white: the harsh light, the deep shadow, the graphic frame. The technique is the exposure for the highlights — the hunter lets the shadows fall where they may. The subject discipline is the graphic: the hunt favors the bold shape, the strong line, the unapologetic dark. The composition craft is the abstraction — the contrast reduces the world to design. The hunt's lesson is the light's edge: the harsh light that ruins the portrait makes the graphic. The shadow is the ink; the light is the paper.
key_points: Favor bold shapes and strong lines.
Contrast reduces the world to design.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The High Contrast Hunt

JAH-PHO-010074.title: The Quiet Moment Hunt
JAH-PHO-010074.summary: The pause between: the quiet hunt.

details.subject: The Quiet Moment Hunt
details.note: The quiet moment hunt seeks the pause between: the empty chair, the folded hands, the held breath. The technique is the invisibility — the hunter becomes furniture, and the moment arrives unposed. The subject discipline is the small: the quiet lives in the details, not the spectacles. The composition craft is the restraint — the quiet frame whispers. The hunt's lesson is the attention: the quiet moments are everywhere, and the camera teaches the noticing. The pause is the photograph; the noticing is the hunt.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Quiet Moment Hunt

JAH-PHO-010075.title: The Panorama Hunt
JAH-PHO-010075.summary: The wide world: the panoramic hunt.

details.subject: The Panorama Hunt
details.note: The panorama hunt takes the wide world: the vista too broad for one frame, stitched from many. The technique is the overlap — the hunter shoots the sequence with generous overlap, level and steady. The subject discipline is the horizon: the panorama needs the line that holds it together. The composition craft is the ends — the panorama's edges must earn their place. The hunt's lesson is the breadth: the wide frame teaches the wide seeing. The Year of Hunts closes with the widest view. The vista is the subject; the stitching is the craft.
key_points: The wide frame teaches wide seeing.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Panorama Hunt
